        "contents": "    }\n    \n    // Tracking-Modus-Text\n    private var trackingModeText: String {\n        if isInBackground {\n            return NSLocalizedString(\"Tracking mode: Battery saving (only significant movements)\", comment: \"Tracking mode text for background mode\")\n        } else {\n            return NSLocalizedString(\"Tracking mode: Live (GPS)\", comment: \"Tracking mode text for foreground mode\")\n        }\n    }\n    \n    // Ist die App im Hintergrund?\n    private var isInBackground: Bool {\n        UIApplication.shared.applicationState == .background\n    }\n    \n    // Log der letzten Updates (Dummy-Implementierung, sollte mit echten Daten aus LocationManager ersetzt werden)\n    private var updateLog: [LocationManager.UpdateLogEntry] {\n        locationManager.updateLog\n    }\n\n    private func speedText(for location: CLLocation) -&gt; String {\n        let metersPerSecond = location.speed\n        if metersPerSecond &gt;= 0 {\n            let kilometersPerHour = metersPerSecond * 3.6\n            return String(format: \"%.1f km/h\", kilometersPerHour)\n        } else {\n            return NSLocalizedString(\"Unknown\", comment: \"Unknown speed value in Location Tracking Details\")\n        }\n    }\n\n    private var batteryLevelText: String {\n        let device = UIDevice.current\n        let wasMonitoringEnabled = device.isBatteryMonitoringEnabled\n        if !wasMonitoringEnabled { device.isBatteryMonitoringEnabled = true }\n        defer { if !wasMonitoringEnabled { device.isBatteryMonitoringEnabled = false } }\n        let level = device.batteryLevel\n        if level &lt; 0 {\n            return NSLocalizedString(\"Unknown\", comment: \"Unknown battery level in Location Tracking Details\")\n        }\n        let percent = Int(level * 100)\n        return \"\\(percent) %\"\n    }\n\n    private func altitudeText(for location: CLLocation) -&gt; String {\n        let verticalAccuracy = location.verticalAccuracy",

                  "lineNumber": 15,
                  "content": "/// Computes a ghost/predicted position along a route, optionally weighting by known device speed."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 16,
                  "content": "/// If speed is provided (in m/s) and timestamp is available, the progress is adjusted from time"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 18,
                  "content": "/// Speed values below the threshold are ignored to filter out GPS noise from stationary devices."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 20,
                  "content": "    /// Minimum speed threshold in m/s to consider device as moving."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 23,
                  "content": "    static let speedThreshold: Double = 1.5 // m/s"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 28,
                  "content": "    ///   - knownDeviceSpeed: Optional remote device speed in meters per second."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 30,
                  "content": "    ///   - knownUserSpeed: Optional local device speed in meters per second."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 34,
                  "content": "    static func ghost(for route: MKRoute, deviceTimestamp: Date?, knownDeviceSpeed: Double?, userTimestamp: Date?, knownUserSpeed: Double?, now: Date = Date(), isRouteReversed: Bool = false) -&gt; (MKPolyline, MKPolyline, CLLocationCoordinate2D, Double)? {"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 38,
                  "content": "        // Only use speeds above the threshold to filter out GPS noise from stationary devices"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 39,
                  "content": "        let deviceSpeed = usableSpeed(knownDeviceSpeed)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 40,
                  "content": "        let userSpeed = usableSpeed(knownUserSpeed)"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 42,
                  "content": "        // Use the speed/timestamp of the journey start to keep progress aligned to route direction."
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 43,
                  "content": "        let primarySpeed = isRouteReversed ? deviceSpeed : userSpeed"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 57,
                  "content": "        if let speed = primarySpeed {"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 60,
                  "content": "                distanceFromStart = min(totalDistance, max(0, elapsed * speed))"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 62,
                  "content": "                // Without a timestamp we cannot project using speed; fall back to travel time"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 84,
                  "content": "    private static func usableSpeed(_ speed: Double?) -&gt; Double? {"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 85,
                  "content": "        guard let speed, speed.isFinite else { return nil }"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 86,
                  "content": "        return speed &gt;= speedThreshold ? speed : nil"
                }
              ]

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"                  \\\"content\\\": \\\"I'm considering the configuration that includes an array of deviceIDs for all known devices. The widget loader seems to only request the primary device and its own, which could lead to two separate network calls if there are multiple widgets for different devices. One possible optimization would be to modify the loader so that it requests all deviceIDs when multiple widgets exist. This approach could ensure that cached payloads and snapshots are available for all devices, speeding up the process. It seems this limitation might be due to WidgetKit constraints.\\\"\""

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"I'm considering the configuration that includes an array of deviceIDs for all known devices. The widget loader seems to only request the primary device and its own, which could lead to two separate network calls if there are multiple widgets for different devices. One possible optimization would be to modify the loader so that it requests all deviceIDs when multiple widgets exist. This approach could ensure that cached payloads and snapshots are available for all devices, speeding up the process. It seems this limitation might be due to WidgetKit constraints.\""

                  "lineNumber": 9026,
                  "content": "+        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;amp;#96; constructs the &amp;amp;#96;TabView&amp;amp;#96; and hosts &amp;amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;amp;#96;, &amp;amp;#96;iPhone_Gro [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9116,
                  "content": "+            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 9131,
                  "content": "+            \"text\": \"- &amp;amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;amp;#96;.\","

                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },

                },

                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                }

                  "lineNumber": 8598,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 8688,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","

                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","

                  "lineNumber": 24804,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"

              "matches": [
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3213,
                  "content": "        \"contents\": \"# miataru App – Feature and Developer Guide\\n\\nThis document lists all features offered by the miataru iOS app. Each item is described twice: once for **users** and once for **developers**. The descriptions also outline how the feature behaves in the interface so the flow from view to view is clear.\\n\\n## App Navigation and Views\\n**For users:**\\n- The app launches to a tab bar with **Devices**, **Groups**, **QR**, and **Settings** tabs. Each tab retains its own navigation stack, so returning to a tab restores where you left off.\\n- Tapping a device or group drills into dedicated map screens, while the QR tab always displays your personal code for quick sharing.\\n\\n- On iPad, you can open a device in a new window from the list or map via context menu, or by dragging the item toward the screen edge.\\n\\n**For developers:**\\n- &amp;#96;iPhone_RootView&amp;#96; constructs the &amp;#96;TabView&amp;#96; and hosts &amp;#96;iPhone_DevicesView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_GroupsView&amp;#96;, &amp;#96;iPhone_MyD [... omitted end of long line]"
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3303,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- When supported by your device/client, the app also submits altitude (above sea level), speed, and battery level with location updates.\","
                },
                {
                  "lineNumber": 3318,
                  "content": "            \"text\": \"- &amp;#96;LocationManager&amp;#96; publishes the current location, permission state, server update status, altitude, speed, battery level (when available), and a log of recent updates. It switches between high‑accuracy updates in the foreground and significant‑change monitoring in the background, requests authorization when needed, and uploads data using &amp;#96;MiataruAPIClient&amp;#96;.\","
                }
              ]
            },
            {

                  "content": "                  \"content\": \"The patch removed the initial elapsed variable causing undefined usage in fallback; I’ll restore elapsed computation using device and user timestamps with priority on device, then user, else zero.         "contents": "    private func updateTrackingMode() {\n        let state = UIApplication.shared.applicationState\n        let status = locationManager.authorizationStatus\n        debugLog(\"updateTrackingMode called, state: \\(state.rawValue), status: \\(status.rawValue), isTracking: \\(isTracking)\")\n        switch status {\n        case .authorizedAlways, .authorizedWhenInUse:\n            if isTracking {\n                if state == .active {\n                    startHighAccuracyUpdates()\n                } else {\n                    startSignificantChangeUpdates()\n                }\n            } else {\n                // Ensure updates are stopped but preserve user's tracking preference flag\n                stopHighAccuracyUpdates()\n                stopSignificantChangeUpdates()\n            }\n        case .notDetermined:\n            // Do not reset isTracking while the user has not decided yet\n            break\n        case .denied, .restricted:\n            // Explicitly stop tracking if permission is denied/restricted\n            stopTracking()\n            // Update the setting to reflect the actual permission state\n            if settings.trackAndReportLocation {\n                settings.trackAndReportLocation = false\n            }\n        @unknown default:\n            stopHighAccuracyUpdates()\n            stopSignificantChangeUpdates()\n        }\n    }\n    \n    private func startHighAccuracyUpdates() {\n        debugLog(\"Calling startHighAccuracyUpdates\")",

Properties\n    @Published var disableDeviceAutolock: Bool {\n        didSet { defaults.set(disableDeviceAutolock, forKey: Keys.disableDeviceAutolock) }\n    }\n    @Published var indicateAccuracyOnMap: Bool {\n        didSet { defaults.set(indicateAccuracyOnMap, forKey: Keys.indicateAccuracyOnMap) }\n    }\n    @Published var groupsZoomToFit: Bool {\n        didSet { defaults.set(groupsZoomToFit, forKey: Keys.groupsZoomToFit) }\n    }\n    @Published var miataruServerURL: String {\n        didSet {\n            defaults.set(miataruServerURL, forKey: Keys.miataruServerURL)\n            WidgetDataSyncCoordinator.syncWidgetConfig(\n                serverURL: miataruServerURL,\n                deviceIDs: KnownDeviceStore.shared.devices.map { $0.DeviceID },\n                ownDeviceID: thisDeviceIDManager.shared.deviceID\n            )\n        }\n    }\n    @Published var trackAndReportLocation: Bool {\n        didSet { \n            defaults.set(trackAndReportLocation, forKey: Keys.trackAndReportLocation)\n            // Check location permissions when tracking is enabled\n            if trackAndReportLocation {\n                checkAndRequestLocationPermissions()\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    @Published var saveLocationHistoryOnServer: Bool {\n        didSet { defaults.set(saveLocationHistoryOnServer, forKey: Keys.saveLocationHistoryOnServer) }\n    }\n    @Published var locationDataRetentionTime: Int {\n        didSet { defaults.set(String(locationDataRetentionTime), forKey: \"location_data_retention_time\") }\n    }\n    @Published var mapType: Int {\n        didSet { defaults.set(String(mapType), forKey: Keys.mapType) }\n    }\n    @Published var mapUpdateInterval: Int {\n        didSet { defaults.set(String(mapUpdateInterval), forKey: Keys.mapUpdateInterval) }",

        "contents": "            DeviceLocationCacheStore.shared.setLocation(\n                for: thisDeviceIDManager.shared.deviceID,\n                latitude: location.coordinate.latitude,\n                longitude: location.coordinate.longitude,\n                accuracy: location.horizontalAccuracy,\n                timestamp: location.timestamp,\n                batteryLevel: batteryPercent,\n                altitude: altitudeValue,\n                speed: speedValue\n            )\n            self.sendLocationToServer(location)\n            self.addUpdateLogEntry(mode: mode)\n        }\n    }\n    func locationManager(_ manager: CLLocationManager, didChangeAuthorization status: CLAuthorizationStatus) {\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            self.authorizationStatus = status\n            // If permission is denied or restricted, update the setting to reflect the actual state\n            if status == .denied || status == .restricted {\n                if settings.trackAndReportLocation {\n                    debugLog(\"Location permission denied/restricted, setting trackAndReportLocation to false\")\n                    settings.trackAndReportLocation = false\n                }\n            }\n            if status == .authorizedWhenInUse,\n               settings.trackAndReportLocation,\n               !hasRequestedAlwaysAuthorization {\n                // Escalate to Always once, if user opted-in to tracking\n                debugLog(\"Authorized WhenInUse. Requesting Always authorization…\")\n                hasRequestedAlwaysAuthorization = true\n                self.locationManager.requestAlwaysAuthorization()\n            }\n            self.updateTrackingMode()\n        }\n    }\n    func locationManager(_ manager: CLLocationManager, didFailWithError error: Error) {\n        Task { @MainActor in\n            self.serverUpdateStatus = .failed(error.localizedDescription)\n        }\n    }\n} \n\nextension Notification.Name {\n    static let didSendOwnLocationUpdate = Notification.Name(\"didSendOwnLocationUpdate\")",
